verdict.line: You lose if Aatrox lands Infernal Chains into his triple Q swing before level 6; you win if you survive to Essence Reaver and let Parrrley poke and Grog-Soaked Blade poison take over.

brief.thesis: Aatrox wins every short trade because his kit is built to force one: Infernal Chains punishes you for standing still, Umbral Dash closes the gap for free, and Deathbringer Stance turns one of his autos into a percent-health nuke with a heal attached. Gangplank's 51.3% win rate over 3880 games isn't won in lane — it's won by surviving lane with Doran's Blade sustain and Remove Scurvy, then flipping the matchup once Essence Reaver and The Collector come online and Parrrley starts out-ranging everything he has.

theirWindow.what: Aatrox is hunting for the chain to drag you to its center and chain it into The Darkin Blade's three swings plus an empowered Deathbringer Stance auto. Give up CS near the middle of the wave rather than contest it at his 825-range W.

yourWindow.when: both Infernal Chains and Umbral Dash are down
yourWindow.what: He has no pull and no dash to close distance or escape, so walk up and trade autos to stack Grog-Soaked Blade poison, or just land a free Parrrley (Q) at 625 range since he can't punish the step-up.

start.why: 51.2% win rate over 3374 games as the dominant 75.1% pick — the extra HP and sustain matter against a champion whose entire early kit is built around forcing melee trades you don't want.

boots.why: 52.2% win rate over 1811 games, 47.4% pick — flat physical damage reduction blunts both his normal autos and the empowered Deathbringer Stance hit in extended trades.

core.why: The mana and attack-speed spike lets you spam Parrrley (5s cooldown) freely while farming and poking, which is the whole engine of this matchup's comeback.
Lets low-health execute threats from Parrrley's killing-blow bonus actually convert, and is part of the 59.8% win rate path into Infinity Edge over 400 games.
Completes the highest win-rate (59.8%, 14% pick) core path and turns Grog-Soaked Blade poison plus crit autos into real DPS once you're past the laning phase.

situational.when: his Umbral Dash and World Ender healing are keeping him alive through your damage
he's building armor or health to shrug off your crit items
you need the extra survivability to not get deleted by a chained all-in before level 9

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks a second source of sustained burn on top of Grog-Soaked Blade's poison, which matters here because you're intentionally avoiding straight auto trades and need damage that lands even when you're kiting Parrrley pokes instead of standing in melee range.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is the standard 51.2% win rate, 94.4% pick combo — Ignite directly cuts the healing from Deathbringer Stance, Umbral Dash, and World Ender that otherwise lets Aatrox win extended trades, and Flash is your answer to getting hooked by Infernal Chains.

playing.title: Poke, don't auto-trade
playing.detail: Use Parrrley (Q) at 625 range to harass and farm instead of standing in his 25-range melee kit. Standing still to trade autos invites the empowered Deathbringer Stance hit, which deals bonus magic damage based on your max health and heals him.

playing.title: Track Infernal Chains cooldown
playing.detail: Infernal Chains (W) is a skillshot that drags you to its impact point if you don't clear the zone fast enough, and it's on a 20/18/16/14/12s cooldown depending on his rank. When it's up, give extra space near the middle of the wave.

playing.title: Save Remove Scurvy for the chain
playing.detail: W (Remove Scurvy) clears any crowd control on you and heals you, so the instant Infernal Chains lands, use it to deny the second pull and the follow-up Q swings. It only sits at rank 1 (22s cooldown) for a long stretch under this skill order, so don't waste it on a cosmetic self-heal.

playing.title: Punish a spent Umbral Dash
playing.detail: Umbral Dash (E) heals him passively whenever he damages you, and its dash is on a 9/8/7/6/5s cooldown. Once he's used it to engage, he has no way to close distance again — that's your cue to walk up and stack poison.

playing.title: Play passive through his level 6-8 spike
playing.detail: World Ender (R) fears nearby minions and grants him bonus AD, healing, and move speed on activation starting at level 6, with cooldown dropping to 80s by rank 3. Avoid committing to extended fights in this window until Essence Reaver is online.

playing.title: Flip the lane at Essence Reaver
playing.detail: Your trades turn once Essence Reaver and The Collector are up — the crit scaling on Parrrley plus Grog-Soaked Blade poison starts outdamaging his short combo, which is when his measured lane advantage actually starts to erode.

playing.title: Zone his dash with Cannon Barrage
playing.detail: Drop Cannon Barrage (R) on him the moment he commits Umbral Dash into you — the slow from the barrage denies him a second dash to disengage once it comes off cooldown, turning a close fight into a kill.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the trade-pattern and timing analysis explaining why those numbers look this way is this brief's own read on the two kits.

stats.opponentTip: Stack up on Grasp of the Undying while laning, but be careful of his (R). A single mistake on [E] can cost you a Summoner’s Spell or a death.
